drhp.business: The Company provides a comprehensive suite of business travel services including air ticketing, hotel bookings, mobility solutions, visa facilitation and related travel services to corporate clients seeking cost control, compliance, duty-of-care management and improved traveller experience. Alongside corporate travel it runs a MICE (meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions) business managing domestic and outbound programmes, an outbound and domestic leisure business built on curated products and personalised itineraries, and a corporate chauffeur-driven car rental operation. risks.note: Management states the operating landscape shifted materially in the latter part of the year as tariff measures, escalating trade tensions, Rupee volatility and geopolitical developments including the conflict in West Asia heightened uncertainty; for the travel industry these influenced consumer sentiments, fuel prices, route economics and cross-border mobility.
risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption to travel demand and cross-border mobility

risks.note: The same paragraph identifies fuel prices and route economics as the channel through which external shocks reach the travel industry, a structural cost/pricing exposure for a company whose revenue is built on air ticketing and chauffeur-driven mobility.
risks.risk: Fuel price and route economics exposure

risks.note: Volatility in the Indian Rupee is named among the factors that materially shifted the operating landscape - relevant given the outbound leisure and outbound MICE exposure.

Domestic air traffic growth slowed to 3.48% year-on-year in 2025 from 6.12% in 2024 (DGCA); management notes the pace of expansion moderated amid external uncertainties and operational constraints, and the Company's travel management volumes track this base.
risks.risk: Moderating growth in Indian domestic air traffic

risks.note: Management states geopolitical tensions and travel-related disruptions have affected outbound event timelines and international delegate participation, leaving the outbound half of the MICE business exposed even while domestic MICE stays resilient.
risks.risk: Outbound MICE and international delegate participation disruption

risks.note: Demand for Europe and parts of the Middle East was impacted by geopolitical developments and air connectivity constraints, concentrating outbound leisure performance in short-haul destinations such as Singapore, Thailand, Bali, Malaysia and Vietnam.
risks.risk: Air connectivity constraints on long-haul outbound leisure

risks.note: Per the GBTA Business Travel Outlook cited by management, global business travel spending growth moderated to approximately 7% in 2025 from around 10% in 2024, reflecting continued uncertainty around global trade policies and economic conditions, with normalisation expected over the medium term after 2026.

sk.overview: The overnight ocean and coastal cruise industry in India is a nascent, high-growth segment of cruise tourism. Per the issuer-commissioned CRISIL Report (May 2026), the domestic market was valued at approximately Rs 8,301 million in Fiscal 2025 (up from Rs 5,764 million in Fiscal 2020, ~8% CAGR) but is estimated to have declined ~12% to Rs 7,325 million in Fiscal 2026 amid macro/fuel/geopolitical headwinds, before a projected sharp expansion.
